concepts.name: VisuospatialReasoning
concepts.description: Reasoning with visuospatial knowledge that combines visual information (what) and spatial information (where). Causality is often implicit, allowing inference of hidden relationships from visual scenes such as in the Duncker radiation problem or engineering diagrams.

concepts.name: SystemsThinking
concepts.description: Understanding systems as composed of interacting components across multiple levels of abstraction. Involves reasoning about invisible processes derived from visible structures, enabling analysis of behaviors in ecological, mechanical, or organizational systems.

concepts.name: DesignThinking
concepts.description: An approach to solving open-ended, ill-defined problems where both problem and solution co-evolve

concepts.name: Creativity
concepts.description: The ability to produce results that are novel, non-obvious, and desirable.

concepts.name: AIEthics
concepts.description: The study of moral and societal implications of artificial intelligence, including its impact on employment, defense, autonomy, and the definition of human-machine boundaries. Raises questions of responsibility, alignment, and civil rights for intelligent systems.

concepts.name: VisualPart
concepts.description: Visible objects, shapes, and perceptual details in a scene.

concepts.name: SpatialPart
concepts.description: Arrangement and geometric relations between visual elements.

concepts.name: VisuoSpatialContent
concepts.description: Combination of visual and spatial information used for reasoning.

concepts.name: RepresentationMode
concepts.description: Type of representation used in reasoning.

concepts.name: PropositionalRepresentation
concepts.description: Symbolic representation with entities and relations expressed as propositions.

concepts.name: AnalogicalRepresentation
concepts.description: Structural representation maintaining spatial or relational correspondence between domains.

concepts.name: CausalPattern
concepts.description: Generalized cause–effect schema extracted from examples.

concepts.name: ProblemContext
concepts.description: Context or situation in which reasoning or problem solving occurs.

concepts.name: VisuoSpatialSolution
concepts.description: Solution generated from visuospatial reasoning or analogy.

concepts.name: System
concepts.description: Set of components forming a functional whole.

concepts.name: StructureModel
concepts.description: Model representing physical components and visible interconnections of a system.

concepts.name: BehaviorModel
concepts.description: Model of internal processes or state transitions in a system.

concepts.name: FunctionModel
concepts.description: Model describing intended outcomes or purposes of a system.

concepts.name: SBFModel
concepts.description: Integrated Structure–Behavior–Function representation linking structure, behavior, and function. Also referred as SBF or FBS Ontology

concepts.name: DesignGoal
concepts.description: Desired objective or requirement in a design problem.

concepts.name: Constraints
concepts.description: Limitations or boundary conditions on design or reasoning.

concepts.name: ProposedDesign
concepts.description: Generated artifact or solution proposed through design reasoning.

concepts.name: DesignPattern
concepts.description: Reusable schema or principle that captures effective design structure.

Assertions.name: consistent
Assertions.description: Ensures the solution aligns with problem constraints.

Assertions.name: aligned
Assertions.description: Ensures structure, behavior, and function are coherent in SBF.

Assertions.name: addresses
Assertions.description: Evaluates whether the proposed design satisfies its goal.

Assertions.name: BSF
Assertions.description: Abbreviation for Structure Behavior Function Modeling
